subject.title: feat: add lease-bound metadata to session spawns

question: Should OpenClaw core permanently own an Agentic OS-specific lease and session metadata RPC contract, or should core provide only a generic extension seam for an external owner/plugin to implement it?
rationale: The branch adds a new public Gateway contract, shared persistent state, and authorization policy. Repository policy places owner-specific behavior in the owner plugin when generic SDK, manifest, or runtime seams can serve it, so this cannot be resolved safely as a mechanical review fix.

options.title: Require an owner-neutral core seam
options.body: Keep generic lease/session extension primitives in core and move Agentic OS-specific RPC names, metadata schema, and orchestration policy to the owning integration.

options.title: Sponsor the core contract
options.body: Accept this as a supported core API, then require an upgrade-safe schema path, explicit protocol/API ownership, and current-head live evidence before merge.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Close or defer the branch until a maintainer defines the external-orchestrator product boundary and long-term API commitment.

recommendation.title: Require an owner-neutral core seam
recommendation.body: Keep generic lease/session extension primitives in core and move Agentic OS-specific RPC names, metadata schema, and orchestration policy to the owning integration.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only directly evidenced contributor for the proposed contract, though a core Gateway owner should be added through normal maintainer routing.
